clippings.speaker: Park Chan-wook
clippings.quote: in a situation where you can imagine I'd find myself very lonely; to have somebody I was very close to was a very reassuring thing. … I had to rely on Chung-hoon.
clippings.title: Interview: Park Chan-Wook Talks STOKER
clippings.context: Park on having Chung beside him for his first English-language film, in a New York interview with The Lady Miz Diva.

clippings.speaker: Park Chan-wook
clippings.quote: to have somebody who I've been collaborating with for a long time, especially when I find myself on a film set where everything had to happen at a much faster pace, I had to have somebody who I was familiar with; we know each other very well. If it wasn't for that fact, I wouldn't have been able to finish this film in the 40-day shoot that it was.
clippings.title: Interview: Park Chan-Wook Talks STOKER
clippings.context: Same interview: Park on why Chung mattered creatively on the fast Hollywood shoot.

clippings.speaker: Park Chan-wook
clippings.quote: Ever since I made Oldboy, I worked with the same cinematographer. Even though we are not co-writing the script, we talk a lot about the story, and from the step of making the storyboard, we are always together.
clippings.title: Interview with Park Chan-wook
clippings.context: Park, interviewed at the Brussels International Fantastic Film Festival, asked how he works with Chung.

clippings.speaker: Chung Chung-hoon
clippings.quote: I've worked with a lot of different film directors but Park Chan-wook is one of the directors who have readily accepted a lot of my ideas. I am really grateful for your comment about my work being beautiful but from my perspective it really is director Park's choosing of specific styles that ultimately made the films what they are.
clippings.title: Chung Chung-hoon: analogue in a digital world
clippings.context: London group interview at the Korean Cultural Centre UK, asked how much of the look of Park's films was his idea.

clippings.speaker: Chung Chung-hoon
clippings.quote: he gave me the job of cinematographer on Oldboy without him ever having seen any of my work … After Oldboy, Park Chan-wook finally saw my earlier movie and said, "What on earth was that?"… He hated it and perhaps if he had seen that film before he spoke to me he would never have employed me.
clippings.title: Chung Chung-hoon: analogue in a digital world
clippings.context: Same group interview: how Park hired him for Oldboy on an editor's recommendation.

clippings.speaker: Chung Chung-hoon
clippings.quote: With director Park, we often show each other various images and in fact he is still constantly sending me pictures. … There is not text or explanation at all, just a photo. … All joking aside, it does allow me to know what the director is thinking and how he is working on a script.
clippings.title: Chung Chung-hoon: analogue in a digital world
clippings.context: Same group interview: Chung showing reference images Park emails him in the middle of the night.

clippings.speaker: Chung Chung-hoon
clippings.quote: To them, I am not just a cinematographer but also someone to discuss the story and characters with. Especially the time I spent with PARK has been tremendously helpful for me.
clippings.title: CHUNG Chung-hoon, Cinematographer of It
clippings.context: Korean Film Council email interview around It, asked about working with Park and his Hollywood directors.

notes: Park rarely talks about Chung at length in English; ScreenAnarchy (Stoker) is the richest source. The IndieWire 2025 piece only says Chung was too busy for No Other Choice, so I left it out.
